name: Shibuya Crossing at night
short_description: Frame the moving scramble, illuminated buildings and street energy from the edge of the public pedestrian area.

shooting_area.name: North edge public sidewalk near the crossing
shooting_area.standing_instruction: Use the public sidewalk edge only. Do not stop inside the crossing, step into vehicle lanes, block tactile paving or hold position against pedestrian flow.
shooting_area.verification_note: The suggested sidewalk area is a safer editorial alternative to reproducing a camera position inside the scramble. It has not been checked on site.

shot_guide.bearing_method: adapted from the 174-degree heading in the reference photo metadata to an approximate sidewalk area
shot_guide.phone_camera_suggestion: Start with the main 1x camera and hold your position at the sidewalk edge. Crop later instead of moving into the crossing for a tighter frame.
shot_guide.composition_instruction: Keep the street horizon level, place the crossing flow across the lower third and leave room above for the illuminated building faces.
shot_guide.composition_short_instruction: Hold the crossing on the lower third and keep the bright buildings upright.
shot_guide.expected_view: A dense pedestrian foreground with illuminated Shibuya buildings and signage behind it.
field_checks_needed: Verify whether the 174-degree view remains practical after station-area changes.
Compare 24 mm and 35 mm framing from the sidewalk edge.
Observe pedestrian density across multiple signal cycles.

timing_and_light.primary_recommendation: Try approximately 10 to 35 minutes after sunset for a blue-to-dark sky and illuminated signs. Screen content and brightness change continuously.
timing_and_light.alternate_recommendation: A rainy evening can add reflections but also increases slip risk and umbrella congestion; this has not been field tested.
timing_and_light.lighting_direction_note: The shot relies primarily on surrounding artificial light rather than a specific sun angle.
timing_and_light.subject_lighting_note: Advertising displays change and should not be treated as a repeatable part of the composition.

access.cost_note: GO TOKYO lists the crossing as free. Paid observation facilities are not part of this street-level guide.
access.published_hours: The crossing is a working public intersection; access changes with traffic signals, events and station operations.

accessibility.summary: The exact step-free route from a station exit to the suggested sidewalk has not been verified.
accessibility.note: Shibuya Station is complex; follow current station accessibility signs and allow extra time.

conditions.crowd_note: GO TOKYO describes very large pedestrian volumes and warns photographers not to walk into people. Density varies by time and event.
conditions.safety_note: Remain alert to signals, vehicles, bicycles, tactile paving and fast-moving pedestrian flows. Never stop in the active crossing.

rules_and_respect.site_type: active public intersection and station forecourt
guidance: Pedestrians, signals and transport operations take priority over photography.
Do not stop in the crossing or obstruct tactile paving and station exits.
Avoid making identifiable strangers the subject of the image without permission.
Do not use a tripod in the moving pedestrian area.
Keep bags and equipment close to your body.
Follow police, station staff and event-control instructions immediately.
rules_and_respect.editorial_rule: ViewRoam must not encourage users to recreate the reference camera position inside the active scramble.

live_conditions.title: Use the sidewalk, not the crossing
live_conditions.message: The reference image records a moment in pedestrian flow. ViewRoam's pin deliberately points to an approximate sidewalk area and does not authorize stopping in the scramble.

seasonal_notes.note: Mild evenings can bring dense visitor traffic; wait through several signal cycles.
Blue hour is later and heat can increase fatigue in crowded conditions.
Clear evenings can produce stronger building contrast and color.
Earlier darkness makes the night composition easier, while holiday periods can add exceptional crowding.
